cases.purpose: With real uid/gid 3001 and effective uid/gid 3002 (and supplementary groups 4000,4001) id -ru/-rg print the real IDs, -u/-g the effective IDs, the default output carries euid=/egid= fields, and id -G lists the real gid, then the effective gid, then the supplementary groups, all identical to GNU id.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 id run by the reference bash side in the same kernel credential state, created by util-linux setpriv (--ruid/--euid/--rgid/--egid/--groups) and started with bash -p so the shell keeps its effective ids.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of each id invocation's output and status inside the credential-split shell, with private passwd/group rows bind-mounted over /etc/passwd and /etc/group.
cases.script:
P=$PWD
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers
cat > "$P/passwd.fx" <<'X'
root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash
alice:x:3001:3001:Alice:/tmp/parity-case/home-alice:/bin/bash
bob:x:3002:3002:Bob:/tmp/parity-case/no-such-home:/bin/bash
X
cat > "$P/group.fx" <<'X'
root:x:0:
alice:x:3001:alice
bob:x:3002:
staff:x:4000:alice
wheel:x:4001:alice,bob
ops:x:5000:
X
/usr/bin/mount --bind "$P/passwd.fx" /etc/passwd || echo "MOUNT-FAIL passwd"
/usr/bin/mount --bind "$P/group.fx" /etc/group || echo "MOUNT-FAIL group"
/usr/bin/mkdir -m 755 "$P/home-alice"
snap() { local l; set -f; while IFS= read -r l; do case $l in Uid:*|Gid:*|Groups:*|NoNewPrivs:*) echo $l;; esac; done < /proc/$BASHPID/status; set +f; }

run() { /usr/bin/setpriv --ruid=3001 --euid=3002 --rgid=3001 --egid=3002 --groups=4000,4001 "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -p -c "$1" 2>&1; }
for q in 'id -ru' 'id -rg' 'id -u' 'id -g' 'id -run' 'id -rgn' 'id -un' 'id -gn' 'id' 'id -G' 'id -Gn' 'id -Gr' 'id -Grn'; do
  out=$(run "$q"); rc=$?; echo "$q => $out (rc=$rc)"
done

cases.purpose: As root nice -n N with a negative N lowers the child's niceness by exactly N (clamped to -20), composes with a nested nice, and returns the child's exit status, as GNU nice does.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils 9.7 nice run by the reference bash side as uid 0; the child /usr/bin/nice prints the niceness it inherited.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of each invocation's output and status.
cases.script:
for n in -1 -5 -19 -20 -40 5; do out=$(nice -n $n /usr/bin/nice 2>&1); echo "nice -n $n => $out (rc=$?)"; done
out=$(nice -n -4 /usr/bin/nice -n 2 /usr/bin/nice 2>&1); echo "nested => $out"
nice -n -3 /bin/bash -c 'exit 9'; echo "status=$?"
out=$(nice -n -3 /usr/bin/nice -n -2 /bin/bash -c 'kill -TERM $$' 2>&1); echo "signal rc=$?"

cases.purpose: chrt applies SCHED_FIFO and SCHED_RR with valid priorities 1, 10, 50 and 99 to the command it execs, observed by the child's own sched_getscheduler/sched_getparam, and with -R the reset-on-fork flag is set on the child while a grandchild forked from a FIFO/RR (and from a negative-nice) parent reverts to SCHED_OTHER priority 0 with niceness 0.
cases.oracle: util-linux 2.41 chrt run by the reference bash side as uid 0; an independent Python child reads sched_getscheduler/sched_getparam (the Linux system calls) and its forked grandchild does the same.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of the child's and grandchild's policy, reset flag, priority and niceness lines for each invocation and of each exit status.
cases.script:
P=$PWD

cat > "$P/obs.py" <<'X'
import os, sys
def fmt(tag, pid=0):
    p = os.sched_getscheduler(pid)
    print('%s policy=%d reset=%s prio=%d' % (tag, p & ~0x40000000, bool(p & 0x40000000), os.sched_getparam(pid).sched_priority))
fmt('child')
if sys.argv[1:] == ['fork']:
    pid = os.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        fmt('grandchild')
        print('grandchild nice=%d' % os.nice(0))
        os._exit(0)
    os.waitpid(pid, 0)
X

for spec in '-f 1' '-f 10' '-f 50' '-f 99' '-r 1' '-r 50' '-r 99' '-R -f 10' '-R -r 99'; do
  out=$(chrt $spec /usr/bin/python3 "$P/obs.py" 2>&1); echo "chrt $spec => $out (rc=$?)"
done
for spec in '-R -f 10' '-R -r 20'; do
  out=$(chrt $spec /usr/bin/python3 "$P/obs.py" fork 2>&1); echo "fork chrt $spec => $out"
done
out=$(nice -n -5 chrt -R -f 10 /usr/bin/python3 "$P/obs.py" fork 2>&1); echo "fork nice -5 chrt -R -f 10 => $out"

cases.purpose: chrt -d with runtime 5 ms, deadline 10 ms and period 16.666666 ms on an owned process succeeds, the kernel's sched_getattr read-back reports policy 6 with exactly those three values and /proc/PID/sched shows the deadline policy; invalid orderings (runtime > deadline, deadline > period) are rejected without changing the parameters.
cases.oracle: util-linux 2.41 chrt run by the reference bash side as uid 0 on an owned sleeping Python process; sched_getattr is called directly through the Linux system call (x86-64 number 315) by an independent Python helper.
cases.comparison: Byte parity of the set status, the system-call read-back, the /proc/PID/sched policy/priority/deadline lines and the two rejection statuses and diagnostics.
cases.script:
P=$PWD
cat > "$P/dl.py" <<'X'
import ctypes, os, sys
pid = int(sys.argv[1])
libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
buf = ctypes.create_string_buffer(56)
r = libc.syscall(315, pid, buf, 56, 0)      # sched_getattr, x86-64
if r != 0:
    print('sched_getattr errno', ctypes.get_errno()); sys.exit(1)
size, policy, flags = ctypes.c_uint32.from_buffer(buf, 0).value, ctypes.c_uint32.from_buffer(buf, 4).value, ctypes.c_uint64.from_buffer(buf, 8).value
runtime, deadline, period = (ctypes.c_uint64.from_buffer(buf, o).value for o in (24, 32, 40))
print('policy=%d runtime=%d deadline=%d period=%d' % (policy, runtime, deadline, period))
X
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'import time; time.sleep(25)' & pid=$!
out=$(chrt -d -T 5000000 -D 10000000 -P 16666666 -p 0 $pid 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "set rc=$rc out=[${out//$pid/PID}]"
/usr/bin/python3 "$P/dl.py" $pid
while IFS= read -r l; do case $l in 'policy '*|'prio '*) set -f; echo "proc-sched $l" | /usr/bin/tr -s ' ';; esac; done < /proc/$pid/sched
out=$(chrt -d -T 5000000 -D 4000000 -P 16666666 -p 0 $pid 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "runtime>deadline rc=$rc out=[${out//$pid/PID}]"
out=$(chrt -d -T 5000000 -D 20000000 -P 10000000 -p 0 $pid 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "deadline>period rc=$rc out=[${out//$pid/PID}]"
/usr/bin/python3 "$P/dl.py" $pid
kill $pid; wait $pid 2>/dev/null
echo done
